chains.title: TCF7L2 binding may be reduced on the C allele

links.claim: TCF7L2 is expressed and has a ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT116. Its TCF7-mapped QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref T than alt C, but the modeled site is weak and the result is not direct allele-specific occupancy evidence.
The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the reported activity-mark scores are maxima across biosamples and do not establish activity in HCT116.

POU5F1B is a candidate target based on proximity and L2G scores, but those scores come from low-PIP, non-CRC credible sets and do not establish that this element regulates POU5F1B; no significant GTEx eQTL is reported.
HCT116 is a plausible context because TCF7L2 occupancy and expression are reported there, although allele-specific occupancy at this base has not been shown.
POU5F1B has some colorectal-cancer relevance, but the cited gene-level and separate circRNA evidence does not show that this variant affects POU5F1B or colorectal-cancer risk.

predictions: If TCF7L2 occupies the variant-overlapping site in HCT116, T should show greater TCF7L2 occupancy than C; this prediction is uncertain because the modeled site is weak.

falsified_if: A sensitive allele-specific occupancy assay in HCT116 finds no T-versus-C difference despite confirmed TCF7L2 occupancy at the site.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401265:T>C, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 40 occupied (6 with a strong site), 5 of 103 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 11 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 517 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 5 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.

Here, we perform statistical fine-mapping incorporating tissue-specific epigenetic annotations and massively parallel reporter assays to systematically prioritize functional variants for each CRC risk locus.
